highlights.title: AI Safety Push Raises Antitrust Questions for Anthropic, OpenAI
highlights.description: AI leaders loosely agree to pace development, but China and Trump have something else in mind

highlights.title: Trump’s opposition to AI rules undercuts industry's calls for a slowdown
highlights.description: Anthropic and OpenAI have called for mandatory safety checks to be put in place as fears intensify that AI can soon be too powerful to control.

highlights.title: ChatGPT transcripts are reportedly read by humans to improve responses, including those with personal information — 'Project Lilly' has seen OpenAI hire hundreds of contractors to manually review logs
highlights.description: 404 Media reports that OpenAI has hired hundreds of contractors to evaluate ChatGPT responses manually.

highlights.title: Meta Bulls Bet Stock Will Break Out After Year of Head Fakes
highlights.description: Meta Platforms Inc. shares have been on a rollercoaster ride through 2026, rising and falling as investor belief in the Facebook parent’s status as a player in the artificial intelligence space ebbs and flows.

highlights.title: Microsoft rolls out emergency update for Windows 11's latest patch — recent update causes crashes on AMD graphics, Explorer hang-ups, and broken third-party integrations
highlights.description: Windows September 2026 update brings many long-requested features, but also surfaces fresh bugs — new code crashing AMD, HP, and Lenovo systems and surfaces audio, Explorer, and Remote Desktop problems

highlights.title: Perplexity’s local AI agent comes to Windows, but only for RTX GPUs with at least 24GB of VRAM — Portable Computer brings AI for multistep tasks to compatible PCs
highlights.description: Perplexity and Nvidia released Portable Computer for Windows on Sept. 14, bringing the local-first AI agent to GeForce RTX and RTX PRO GPUs with 24GB or more of VRAM.

highlights.title: New Apple CEO John Ternus attending Emmy Awards (and sporting iPhone Duo)
highlights.description: It’s Emmy Awards night, and John Ternus is in attendance. The new Apple CEO officially took over for Tim Cook two weeks ago, and he’s already doing iPhone Duo product demos for the stars and press. more…

highlights.title: Chip Startup Euclyd, Backed By Ex-ASML CEO, Raises More Than €200 Million
highlights.description: Dutch chip startup Euclyd has raised more than €200 million in funds and named ASML Holding NV’s former Chief Executive Officer Peter Wennink as chairman.

highlights.title: Trump, China Push Back on Calls to Slow AI
highlights.description: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang took a live phone call from Donald Trump during a panel discussion, where Trump dismissed artificial intelligence dangers as a “hoax.” Meanwhile, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson has pushed back against tech leaders' calls to slow frontier AI development. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Apple's Weirdest iTunes Walk-Back Turns 12 Today
highlights.description: 12 years ago today, Apple published a web page with one job: to make a U2 album go away. On September 9, 2014, at Apple's iPhone 6 event, Tim Cook revealed that "Songs of Innocence" would be given to every iTunes customer for nothing. The album was directly linked to accounts, and devices set to "download automatically" got it without asking. available here. ai.title: AI Trade Is in 'Digestion' Phase, JPMorgan's Sundar Says
ai.description: Sitara Sundar, head of alternative investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, discusses the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade. Speaking on Bloomberg Television, she says her firm still has a constructive view on the AI industry in the long run. "We would actually start to lean more into some of the integration and the application layer of artificial intelligence," she adds. (Source: Bloomberg)

ai.title: AI Slowdown Calls Won’t Halt Fundraising, AllianceBernstein Says
ai.description: Calls for a slowdown in artificial intelligence development won’t stop major technology companies from pressing ahead with fundraising and capital spending, according to AllianceBernstein Holding LP fixed-income specialists.

ai.title: Hugging Face Says Good Ethics Can Drive AI Innovation
ai.description: Hugging Face Researcher & Chief Ethics Scientist Margaret Mitchell believes if done well, ethics can drive innovation in artificial intelligence instead of slowing it down. She speaks with Haslinda Amin on "Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)

ai.title: Hugging Face Scientist on Safety Issues With Agentic AI
ai.description: Margaret Mitchell, chief ethics scientist at Hugging Face, warns that autonomous AI agents pose oversight challenges that incumbent firms may be leveraging to restrict competition. She argues that safety, privacy, and security must be built directly into AI architectures rather than treated as trade-offs to frontier progress. (Source: Bloomberg)
